messages:
kyle: heads-up — saw a spike of NaNs in the attention outputs after yesterday's rope/rotary kernel change (PR#3421).

kyle: stack trace attached in the error logs: `RuntimeError: CUDA kernel assert or NaN encountered in attention_dot` — happening on long sequences (>4096) in fp16.

mira: ugh. which change specifically? the precompute cache refactor?

kyle: yeah, we flattened the cos/sin cache and added an in-place cast to fp16 when storing to reduce mem. naive repro below.

kyle: repro (minimal):
```
# repro.py
import torch
from model.ops import apply_rope
x = torch.randn(1, 1, 8192, 64, device='cuda', dtype=torch.half)  # long seq
cos_sin = precompute_cos_sin(8192, 64).to(torch.half)  # previously fp32
out = apply_rope(x, cos_sin)
# sometimes produces NaNs within a few steps
```

jamal: repro confirmed on A100 in our staging pool. NaNs start showing when seq_len > ~4600.

mira: hypothesis: casting the precomputed angles to fp16 at cache-time blows up precision for large position indices, and some fused ops accumulate and hit inf/NaN. we used in-place cast to save memory — that might be the trigger.

nina: another angle — could be buffer reuse across Batches. The cache is shared between threads in the kernel and we do an inplace multiply that assumes freshly allocated buffers. If a stale fp16 buffer has garbage it could underflow/overflow.

jamal: i dug into the PR diff — we do `cos_sin_cache = cos_sin_cache.half_()` before returning. There was a test added that only checks forward correctness for seq<2048. so long seqs were never validated.

mira: short term fix: compute cos/sin in fp32 and keep the cache as fp32. Cast to fp16 at the point of use (not in-place) or use a fused kernel that performs the multiply in fp32 accumulation and casts the final result.

kyle: i pushed a tiny patch to keep cache in fp32 and only `.to(dtype=torch.half)` inside `apply_rope` with a non-inplace cast. PR#3489.

qa-alex: ran unit tests: `pytest tests/ops/test_rope_fp16.py::test_long_seq` — before patch it fails reproducibly; after patch it passes on A100 but still flaky on older Turing cards (probably numeric range differences).

mira: we should add an explicit regression test for seq lengths up to 16k, both fp16 and bf16, and assert no NaNs and relative error vs fp32 < 1e-3 for fp16. I'll open a test PR.

jamal: ops-level note — we should also avoid `half_()` in any shared tensor that might be referenced by other kernels. in-place casts are dangerous when tensors live in caching pools.

nina: also add a flag to the kernel selector: `use_fp32_posenc_cache=true` fallback. That way we can roll out the cached fp16 optimization behind a feature flag and canary it.

kyle: good plan. can we get a quick perf measurement? does keeping cache fp32 blow up VRAM enough to matter?

mira: measurement from staging: keeping cache fp32 increased peak mem by ~3% for 8k seq on A100 with our batch sizes. latency was unchanged within noise. so acceptable for now.

qa-alex: infra: i reproduced the failure on a small v100 node — will add the device matrix to the CI job. we should run the new long-seq tests on both a100-40g, a100-80g, t4, v100.

kyle: rollout plan: merge PR#3489 (keep fp32 cache) -> enable in master -> canary on 5% of hosted inference traffic on dedicated pool with `rope_fp16_cache` flag = false for older hardware -> monitor NaN count, token-latency, mem. fallback to previous kernel on >0.1% NaN rate.

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: 2026-03-20T17:30Z (5% traffic).

mira: tests to add before merge:
- determinism check (seeded) for seq lengths [1024,4096,8192,16384] in {fp16,bf16}
- gradient sanity for transformers with rotary applied (small model)
- allocation/regression test to ensure no inplace half_() is used in cached objects

jamal: i'll add lint that forbids `.half_()` on anything named `*_cache` or that passes through `cache_pool`. simplified rule in the ops linter.

nina: also add a runtime trace point to the kernel selector that logs `posenc_cache_dtype` and `posenc_cache_size` and counts NaNs per device — helps incident debugging.

qa-alex: once merged i'll run the matrix and report back. already ran basic perf vs master; no regression in throughput for our baseline.

kyle: thanks everyone. follow-ups: mira opens test PR, jamal opens linter PR, nina opens selector flag PR. i'll keep the canary monitor up.

infra-bot: alert suppressed — no increased 5xx. will report if NaNs > 0.1%.
